title: gertrud: Age-appropriate proactive healthcare
summary:
The aim of the gertrud program is to provide cross-sector healthcare that is tailored to the age of patients and the associated risks, ensuring individually planned, proactive, multi-professional coordinated patient care for the best possible patient outcome throughout the entire process, from diagnosis to post-operative follow-up care at home.

The Bavarian State Ministry of Health and Care is promoting the multi-professional development of the gertrud program for age-appropriate proactive healthcare for elderly patients undergoing elective surgery, as well as its testing and accompanying evaluation as part of a pilot project at the Musculoskeletal University Center.

The program name, formed as an acronym, is Programm*.

*The first name Gertrud comes from Old High German with the syllable meanings ger = “spear” and trud = “power; strength.” Active risk-adjusted prevention is a powerful spear in age-appropriate healthcare, proactively reducing complications and side effects in elective surgical procedures. Proactive here means planning and acting in a targeted manner in advance, rather than reacting to complications that have already occurred.
conditions: Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances
Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction
Pneumonitis due to solids and liquids

interventions.name: Intervention: preoperative optimization in collaboration with general practitioners specialists, patients, and relatives, risk-adapted inpatient care by a specialized team of evidence-based nurses with the involvement of accompanying persons (“care & accompany”), and systematic delirium screening.
Control: pre-hospital geriatric assessment with multi-professional risk stratification and systematic delirium screening.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Planned non-emergency surgery (urgency > N2), see Appendix, Table 1 for examples of indications
• Expected duration of anesthesia >= 60 min
• Patient capable of giving consent or legal guardian or authorized representative with permission in the area of “health care” if the patient is not capable of giving consent.
Exclusion criteria:
• Preoperative delirium
• Emergency procedures (<N3)
• Intracranial procedures
• Insufficient knowledge of German
